MANAGEMENT OF INTERMEDIATE/LOW RISK CHEST PAIN 
                                       (if the chest pain is considered to be ACS related) 
 
 
Low risk 
Intermediate 
risk 
The HEART Score for Chest Pain in the ED 
History 
* Highly suspicious 
* 2 points 
* Moderately suspicious 
* 1 point 
* Slightly / non-suspicious 
* 0 points 
ECG 
* Significant ST depression 
* 2 points 
* Nonspecific repolarisation 
* 1 point 
* Normal 
* 0 points 
Age 
* ≥ 65 years 
* 2 points 
* > 45 - < 65 years 
* 1 point 
* ≤ 45 years 
* 0 points 
Risk Factors 
* ≥ 3 risk factors 
* 2 points 
* 1 or 2 risk factors 
* 1 point 
* No risk factors 
* 0 points 
Troponin 
* ≥ 3 x normal limit 
* 2 points 
* > 1 - < 3 x normal limit 
* 1 point 
* ≤ normal limit 
* 0 points 
Risk Factors: Diabetes Mellitus, current or recent (<1 month) smoker, 
Hypertension, Hypercholestrolaemia, Family History, Obesity 
Score 0 - 3 (low risk) 
2.5% MACE over next 6 weeks 
Score 4 - 6 (intermediate risk) 
20.3% MACE over next 6 weeks 
Score 7 - 10 (high risk) 
72.7% MACE over next 6 weeks 
MACE = Major Adverse Cardiac Event

1 point for each variable present

Start Adjunctive Treatments 
* Heparin 
   LMWH:  Clexane® 30mg IV stat then 1mg/kg SC after 15 min 
                                             or if no LMWH 
   Heparin: 60IU/kg (max 4000IU) IV stat then infusion with 12IU/kg/hr  
                                           (max 1000IU/hr) 
 
* Thienopyridines 
   Clopidogrel (Plavix®) 300mg stat po 
 
* Statin 
   Simvastatin (Zocor®) 40mg stat po 
 
* β blocker (if no contraindications - see box) 
    Atenolol (Tenormin®) 50mg stat po 
Calculate & document 
TIMI / HEART score 
Refer to cardiology 
Contraindications  
β Blockers 
* Haemodynamic instability 
* Heart failure 
* Pulmonary oedema 
* SBP < 100 mmHg 
* Bradycardia (HR ≤ 60 bpm)  
* AV block 2° or 3° 
* Asthma  
Intermediate/ Low Risk UA 
Normal ECG or non-diagnostic 
  changes in ST segment or t-waves 
* ST deviation < 0.5mm  
* T-wave inversion ≤ 2mm  
Discharge & refer to 
Medical / Cardiology 
OPD within 1 week 
Repeat Trop I & ECG at 6 hours              
(Repeat ECG if pain / vital signs change)
